edits.new: After your last spring frost, plant the rosemary you bought in the sunniest, best-draining spot. Leave about 24 inches between plants for airflow.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (PSU: two feet apart)

edits.new: Set the nursery plant out after the last spring frost, in the sunniest, sharpest-draining spot you have. Space plants about 24 inches apart, and on heavy or humid ground plant on a mound or raised bed.

edits.new: It is time to plant your rosemary. Put it in a sunny, well-draining spot now that frost has passed, leaving about 24 inches between plants, and do not add fertilizer.

edits.new: Your plant-out window is open. Set the nursery plant in full sun in sharply drained soil after the last frost, spacing plants about 24 inches apart. Skip rich compost and fertilizer.

edits.new: Leave about 24 inches between plants. That space lets air move around each one, which helps prevent the leaf problems rosemary can get when it stays damp.

edits.new: Space plants about 24 inches apart for airflow. Good air circulation between plants is one of the simplest ways to head off the foliar disease rosemary can get in damp or crowded conditions.
